title: WorryCourtroomMinigame.cs
summary: The Worry Courtroom: the player puts a worry on trial, sorts facts from guesses, hears a friend, picks a balanced thought and a small plan. Runs on its own in the standalone scene, or as an overlay a Quest opens. Its screen is one UI Toolkit file (WorryCourtroom.uxml / .uss).

notes.text: A QuestMinigame, so the Quest can open it and wait for it just like the breathing exercise.
The trials. One entry hides the case tabs; add more entries and tabs appear. Each case is its own asset.
Every number: strike limit, how much each right answer lowers the worry, how many defence facts are needed, star thresholds.
Every sentence the game writes itself, with {placeholders} where a value is filled in.
On: runs by itself when the scene loads (the standalone scene). Off: waits for Open() and closes when finished — how Episode 1 uses it.
Sorting order of the screen's UI Toolkit document: above the story panels and the pause menu. The screen is only visible while the courtroom is open.
Fires when a case is finished, with the star rating (1-3). Hook stress or story effects here.

notes.match: VisualElement root, stageBox, figureBox, meterFill, strikesBox, tabsBox, stepsBox;
notes.text: The screen's elements, found by name in WorryCourtroom.uxml (edit the layout in UI Builder; keep the names). It is split into parts: the stage and Worry figure, the step bar, and one panel per round (intro, sort, defence, choice, result, recess).

notes.match: void Populate(VisualElement container, AnswerOption[] opts, Func<int, bool> isOk, Func<int, bool> isBad, Action<int> pick, bool locked)
notes.text: Builds the answer buttons into the container in code, in one or two columns depending on how many answers there are (rules.twoColumnThreshold). Style them with the .court-opt rules in the USS and every answer changes.
Embedded means 'opened by a Quest': the result screen shows Continue instead of Next case / Replay.
Called by the Quest.
Freezes the player and pauses the episode timer while the courtroom is up.
Closes the overlay. Finished: tells the Quest it is complete. Closed early: tells it the minigame can be opened again.
The requirement only counts once the case reaches its result screen.
The meter and the Worry figure follow the real value smoothly instead of jumping.
Three moods: scowling, neutral, calm. The thresholds are in Rules.
The Worry literally shrinks as it is answered: the figure's scale follows the worry meter.
A wrong answer: add a strike, shake the stage, and call a Recess when the limit is reached.
Round 1: is this card a checkable fact, or a feeling or a guess? A guess also reveals its thinking trap.
Round 2: pick the real facts that weigh against the worry; wrong picks show why they don't help.
Rounds 3 to 5 share this: the Friend, the Verdict and the Plan are all 'pick the helpful answer'.
Remember when the player said they'd do the plan, because the round reset clears it before the result screen reads it.

notes.match: int Stars() { return totalStrikes <= rules.threeStarsMaxStrikes ? 3 : totalStrikes <= rules.twoStarsMaxStrikes ? 2 : 1; }
notes.text: Stars come from total wrong answers. Everyone gets at least one.
